item.description: The deadly Ebola virus outbreak in DR Congo continues to spread across the vast country despite some success in containing it, aid officials said on Tuesday, in a renewed call for international support to help responders on the ground. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: UN warns Ebola may not have peaked in DR Congo, despite falling cases
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo shows early signs of slowing. Daily infections have decreased from approximately 120 to about 80 cases. However, transmission continues to rise in some areas, officials caution. Mobile data tracks population movements to predict future virus spread. Kisangani has emerged as a key area of concern due to its transport hub status. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Hong Kong visitor arrivals hit post-pandemic monthly high in August
item.description: Hong Kong has recorded its highest monthly number of visitors since the Covid-19 pandemic, provisional official figures show, with authorities attributing August’s total to a series of international conferences and mega-events. The Hong Kong Tourism Board said on Tuesday that the city received 5.46 million visitors across the month, up 6 per cent from a year earlier and the highest monthly total since the pandemic. item.title: How a 26-year-old hacker breached 165 companies and exposed 100 million people
item.description: A man from Canada confessed to orchestrating a massive hacking scheme in 2024, which resulted in the breach of sensitive data from over 165 organizations, affecting billions of records. The perpetrators demanded hefty ransoms and trafficked stolen information on cybercrime platforms. International law enforcement cooperation led to his arrest in Canada, and he has now pled guilty to numerous offenses, awaiting sentencing in October. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Antibody cocktails could steer viruses into evolutionary dead ends
item.description: When a virus mutates, the world usually finds out the hard way. Variants of influenza and SARS-CoV-2 can slip past vaccines and antibody drugs before scientists fully understand what has changed. A new study from Harvard's Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology (CCB) suggests the hard way may not be inevitable. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tomar el café o el té demasiado caliente puede triplicar el riesgo de cáncer de esófago. La clave está en la temperatura
item.description: A día de hoy, el aumento en la preocupación por nuestra salud ha hecho que poco a poco sepamos mucho más sobre aquellos elementos de nuestra vida cotidiana que nos pueden generar una enfermedad como el cáncer. item.title: Supplier to end classroom lunch portioning at Sha Tin school after 39 fall ill
item.description: A lunch supplier will stop portioning meals in classrooms at a Hong Kong primary school following a suspected food poisoning outbreak that hit 39 pupils and staff members last week. Danny Catering Service said in a statement on Sunday to its school partners, parents and teachers that the incident was “isolated” and linked to the school’s portioning arrangement, and did not affect its services at other locations. “To ensure student food safety and avoid potential cross-contamination or... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
